Against warriors, firearms are generally not considered effective.
Keeping up with our movement, no. Piercing our armor, also no. Two basic requirements, and on both the gun is standing outside.

But put one very simple principle into the calculation, and see what happens.
—One shot will not hit? Achha, send ten. Ten will not pierce? Send a hundred.

Concentrated fire can threaten even a warrior.
Presumably that was why gunports were sticking out of the monster's hide in bank after bank. The argument of more, delivered from everywhere.

And yet—

If I knew where the pilot sat in that enormous body, perhaps something could be arranged. Without that knowledge, whether the person lived or died would be left to luck.

An egg-host, I would kill. Right or wrong, I did not ask; that was my decision. To prevent another Silver Star from being born, the host had to be destroyed completely, as quickly as possible. That reason, and no other.

This was different. This one I could not kill. Some guilt it might carry. Probably it had helped destroy the island's environment and threaten the people nearby. Leave it alive, and perhaps the destruction would continue.

Still, therefore I shall judge it myself—no. That convenience was not permitted. Judgment belonged under the law. Bringing the suspect before a court: that was the extent of my authority.

If the law itself could not be trusted, if the opponent abused power like the shogunate, some might approve of punishment by one's own hand. But that was the terrorist's road. I was, after a fashion, police.

Police must be the faithful hands and feet of justice. Not the hands, feet, judge and executioner, all appointed by myself. Measure the guilt, pronounce sentence and kill on my own say-so? No.

認められよう筈はなかった。

　警察は司法の忠実な手足とならねばならない。
　一存で罪を計り裁きを下し殺害するなど、あっては
ならない事である。

Gargett"...And what is that?"
Research Director"............"
Gargett"Director? Since your memory cannot accommodate it, I shall repeat myself. Answering my questions is your obligation—"
Research Director"Dragon-Qi Cannon! Oscillation cannon, if THAT can enter your skull!"
Gargett"Vibrocannon... Yes. I have heard of the proposed weapon."
Gargett"An application of Crus metal-echo, I understand?"
Research Director"Haan. Receive a warrior's metallic voice, and the surface vibrates in tiny movements, right? Somebody had the cheerful thought: why not make this an attack? Research started from there."
Research Director"Turns out, focus an extremely low metallic voice and emit that vibration, and the target heats and burns instantly. We made it work. That is the Dragon-Qi Cannon."
Gargett"Dragon Breath. I see. A considerable achievement, nonetheless."
Research Director"Hmph."
Gargett"Our army studied it as the decisive armament for mobile weapons. Power supply and miniaturization remained unsolved; I hear the project stalled. As a fixed battery, it does not justify the cost."
Gargett"And your solution was to enlarge the mobile weapon instead. Splendidly crude. Only an island people could conceive of it. We civilized men would have left it as a joke."
Research Director"GUOOAAAH!!"
Gargett"Being moved is all very well, Director. The noise is unnecessary."
Research Director"GRATITUDE dikh raha hai tujhe?! This looks like GRATITUDE to you?!"
Gargett"Emotional displays peculiar to barbarian customs do not interest me. Incidentally, Director—"
Research Director"Home. Bas, I want home. Shut the door and think beautiful murder thoughts... Oh, shooting star. Bhagwan, ek hi dua. Kill him, kill him, kill him... Let my pure little wish reach you..."
Gargett"That lump is an armor, whatever else. How was it forged? At such a size... Honestly, I cannot imagine it."
Research Director"...That, I also don't know. Weapons we fitted. The original is a different matter."
Gargett"Oh?"
Research Director"There is a rock cave at the southwest end of the island. Connects to Mount Fuji's wind caves, people say. Or a god uses it when going for a wander. Stories, stories."
Research Director"They found it there. Eight years ago, a folklore survey team. Apparently the islanders had stories about it from long before that."
Research Director"Omiutsushi, or something. Meaning? Pata nahin. Ask one islander, get one explanation. Ask another, now you have two problems."
Gargett"............"
Research Director"Examined it. Several hundred years old, perhaps more than a thousand, and listen to this: a tsurugi for a warrior already wearing a tsurugi. Yes. Everybody was surprised."
Research Director"Armor wearing armor! Nobody had heard of such a thing. Anyway, Rokuhara took control, and research began as 'reinforced exterior for dragoon use', and—"
Research Director"In the end, how to make it, nobody could work out. Chalo, manufacturing is not happening, at least let us operate the one we have. Studied that, and this is what came out. Whole story."
Gargett"Very well. I understand the outline."
Research Director"Glad to hear it."
Gargett"In short, nothing is known. Thank you for an explanation containing no information. A remarkably wasteful use of my time."
Research Director"Wah. Now enjoyment is coming. How much murderous intent can one man hold? You polished little pressure test, we are finding out."

ガーゲット「……あれは、何かね」
研究所長「……」
ガーゲット「所長？ 　君の記憶能力では覚えきれないようだから 改めて通告するが、君には私の質問に答える 義務が――」
研究所長「竜気砲だよ！ 　発振砲って言やぁあんたらにもわかるか」
ガーゲット「発振砲ヴァイブロカノン……。 　確かにその兵器構想は耳にしたことがある」
ガーゲット「劒冑クルスの装甲通信メタルエコーを応用した兵器だとか？」
研究所長「あぁ。 　武者の金打声を受けると、体表が小刻みに 振動するだろ？　その現象を攻撃に利用でき ないかっつー愉快発想から研究が始まって」
研究所長「その結果、極低度の金打声を集束して発振 すると標的を瞬間的に加熱、燃焼させること が可能だって判明したわけさーねー。 　うちでそいつを実用化したのがあの竜気砲」
ガーゲット「竜気ドラゴンブレスか。なるほどな。 　しかし、大したものだ」
研究所長「ふン」
ガーゲット「あれは。我が軍では機動兵器の決定力たる 搭載武装として研究がなされたが、電力供給 と小型化の問題が解決せず頓挫したと聞く。 　砲台運用ではコスト的に見合わんしな」
ガーゲット「それを、機動兵器の方を大型化することで 解決するとは……素晴らしく大雑把な手法だ。 　島国の未開人なればこそだな。我々文明人 であれば冗談の種で済ませてしまうところだ」
研究所長「ぐぉアーーー!!」
ガーゲット「感激するのは良いが騒がしいのは困るな、 所長」
研究所長「そう見えんのかよ!?」
ガーゲット「蛮国の独特な風習に基づく感情表現などに 興味はない。 　ところで所長」
研究所長「もーおうち帰りてー……。 　部屋に籠もって殺害妄想に耽りてぇー…… あっ流れ星……神さまお願い、こいつ殺して 殺して殺して……届けボクの一途な願い……」
ガーゲット「あのでかぶつは曲がりなりにも劔冑だろう。 だが一体、如何なる方法で鍛造したのだ？ 　あそこまで巨大なものを……正直なところ、 まるで想像がつかない」
研究所長「……そいつは俺も知らねぇー。 　あれ、兵装を調えたのは俺らだが、原型ベースは 違うからな」
ガーゲット「ほう？」
研究所長「この島の南西の端に岩屋がある。 　富士山の風穴に通じてるだの、遊行ゆぎょうし給う 神の道だの、色々と曰くのある洞穴なんだが」
研究所長「あれはその奥で発見されたもんだ。 　八年前、民俗学の調査団にな……もっとも 現地人の間じゃ相当昔から語り伝えられてた らしいけど」
研究所長「おみうつし・・・・・、とか言ってたかな。 　意味はわかんねえ。島の連中が言うことも まちまちだ」
ガーゲット「……」
研究所長「で、そいつを調べてみたところ、数百年か、 下手すると千年以上前に造られた――武者に・・・ 着せる劔冑・・・・・だってことが判明したわけよ。 　まあ、みんな驚いたわ」
研究所長「劔冑の上に劔冑を重ねる、なんつー発想は 前代未聞だったからな。 　ともかくそいつは六波羅の管轄に移って、 竜騎兵用強化外装の名で研究が始まってー」
研究所長「けど結局、製造法はわからんかった。 　しゃーねえからこの一騎だけでも運用して みるかってんで、そっちの研究をした結果、 あれが出来たと。まぁそーいうわけですよー」
ガーゲット「なるほど。 　おおよそ理解した」
研究所長「そらよーござんした」
ガーゲット「要するに『何もわからない』という事だな。 　内容の無い説明を感謝する。大変に無駄な 時間を過ごした気分だ」
研究所長「うわーい。 　なんか段々楽しくなってきたよ俺ー。人間 どこまで殺意を抱けるのか挑戦してる感じー」

To permit movement, the joint plates must be thin and leave gaps. Aim for those: one of the standard methods in Futawagakari, single combat between warriors.

The wave grazed my flank, smelling of the road to Yomi. We fled at full speed. Fled, and fled. Distance first; whatever dignity remained could follow later.

Even such a defense it had prepared. Completely outside our calculation. We had to break off and begin again.

Keep fighting without any prospect of winning, and it is poker with your own hand laid open. The opponent will be very happy. That much success you can guarantee.

Research Director"Small fry, we catch before that happens. This fellow? No chance. My hands are up."
Gargett"............"
Gargett"A defective weapon beyond imagination."
Research Director"DEFECTIVE nahin hai! Change the fuel can—the battery—and it works!"
Gargett"Battery?"
Research Director"Heat source. To fly that enormous body. Stop the unit, put in a fresh one, and off it goes again for a while."

Research Director"Unfortunately, obtaining those batteries is difficult. Stock is low. We cannot throw them about freely."
Gargett"But you have them."
Research Director"...Major. Listen. Research is not finished here. After your present excitement also, our work has to continue."
Research Director"For this pointless brawl, you want batteries burned that we cannot easily replace? Thoda samajh, you expense in a uniform! Understand this much!"
Gargett"Use it."
Research Director"...AAAAH!? Bas kar, madarchod! Enough! Tolerated, tolerated, TOLERATED you—and even my heart, generous as imaginary-number space, has a LIM—"

Up, then twisting down to the right, rolling wide to gain distance. Reverse. At the instant the enemy's tracking crossed mine, I cut through, slipped beneath that silver majesty's flank and came out behind, pitching upward.

The G-force was pressing close to what I could bear. My skeleton creaked. A little error in strength or speed and the whole delicate balance would collapse; this useless lump of calcium would be crushed along with it. I knew. The cold sweat running down my back knew also.

No ordinary opponent. The barrage would be licking at my tail, then suddenly it was waiting ahead. Change course—already ahead there also. Dodge again—again ahead, not a hair out of place.

Several times I had escaped only by cutting back behind the attack itself. Teasing the ferryman of the Sanzu, that was what this amounted to. Any moment, some irritated god of death would seize my collar. Bahut ho gaya. Enough running about.

The bullets closed every direction like a cast net. Accelerating through it, I slipped from mesh to mesh.

Ordinary flight would have left us caught. Good that I obeyed the instinct without argument. It had frozen my heart, not my head; the head had remained available for work.

But how long could this continue? Limits were not the enemy's private property. We were unlikely to freeze before it did, but less heat meant less performance from the whole armor.

The moment Muramasa's mobility fell below the enemy's ability to hit us, the answer to that inequality would be settled. And we would not like the answer.

A paper-thin margin. That much had been enough.

I let out a long... very long breath.

But this recovered life was not offering leisure to appreciate it. Now the contest was recovery.

Regain our footing before the enemy. Deliver the finishing blow. Otherwise, next time we would be driven right to the far bank of the Sanzu, no turning back halfway.
